facts.title: Country and period
facts.text: Country: Tunisia (TUN). Annual period 2014–2025, monthly series 2014-01-01 → 2025-12-01. Levels: ADM1, ADM2. Synthetic data: no.

facts.title: National trend
facts.text: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Tunisia changed by +6.0% per year (95% CI: +5.0% to +6.5%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is +4.1% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))

facts.title: Regions
facts.text: Of 264 ADM2 units, 239 show significant growth, 23 are stagnating and 2 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Sfax accounts for 10% of national light. (confidence medium: classification of 264 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10)

facts.title: Convergence
facts.text: Across ADM2 units, light per capita converges: the least-lit units are catching up. (confidence medium: β = −0.014 [−0.026; −0.003], n = 264)

facts.title: Link with GDP
facts.text: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 4.19 in levels (95% CI: 1.02 to 7.36, R² = 0.54, 12 years) and 0.25 in growth rates (CI: −0.06 to 0.56). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.31 (mean absolute error: 2.9 percentage points of growth). (confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (6.34))

facts.title: Shocks
facts.text: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -9.0% (11/2020), return to the pre-shock level after 10 months. (confidence medium: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)

facts.title: Inequality and access
facts.text: The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.27 in 2025 (no significant change since 2014). About 0.07 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (12% of the inhabited population). (confidence medium: sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.07 to 0.07 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection)

facts.title: Industrial zones
facts.text: 125 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 27 heavy industry, 37 business parks & logistics, 30 oil & gas sites and 31 isolated sites to verify. They emit 25.2% of national light (latest year); their light changes by +2.8% per year. Tunis has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: no reference list available to validate the detection)

facts.title: Summer tourism
facts.text: 23 of 264 units show a net summer light excess of at least 10%: Djerba Ajim (Médenine), Djerba Midoun (Médenine), Zarzis (Médenine), Djerba Houmet Souk (Médenine). The median net excess reaches +29% in the most touristic zone. The season index (base 100 = 2019) falls to 83 in 2020 and stands at 128 in 2025. (confidence low: no hotel-night statistics to validate the indicator)

facts.title: Key indicators
facts.text: Annual growth of light = +6.0% (2014–2025, robust slope (Theil–Sen)); Last 12 months vs previous 12 = +4.1% (seasonally adjusted series, up to 12/2025); Light–GDP elasticity = 4.19 (95% CI 1.02 to 7.36 · confidence medium); Gini of light per capita = 0.27 (ADM2 units, 2025); People in the dark = 0.07 M (12% of the inhabited population, 2025); Share of the top region = 10% (Sfax, 2025); Industrial clusters = 125 (25% of national light); Tourist zones = 23 (max. summer excess +29% (Djerba Ajim (Médenine)))

facts.title: Recommendations
facts.text: • Use night-time lights as a leading and subnational indicator, as a complement to — never a replacement for — the national accounts. • Publish regional GDP estimates as experimental statistics, with intervals and a methodological note, after comparison with available regional accounts. • Cross-check the map of populations “in the dark” against grid-connection registers: the average gap with the World Bank access rate is -12 percentage points. • Have the 31 isolated sites checked on high-resolution imagery and complete the official register of industrial zones used as the validation reference. • Monitor the light of industrial clusters monthly as a leading indicator of industrial output, and compare it with the industrial production index where one exists. • Publish the tourist season index right after the summer (VIIRS data are available within weeks), ahead of hotel-night statistics, and recalibrate it on them every year. • Update the dashboard every quarter (monthly VIIRS series) and every year (annual VNL composites).

facts.title: Limitation: What lights measure
facts.text: Upward radiance emitted around 01:30: agriculture, daytime trade, poorly lit services and the rural informal economy are poorly captured.

facts.title: Limitation: Saturation and blooming
facts.text: DMSP saturates in city centres (DN 63) and “blooms” beyond lit areas; VIIRS is much better, but blooming still inflates the lit area of cities.

facts.title: Limitation: Gas flares and isolated sites
facts.text: The automatic mask may remove isolated mines, ports or power plants, and miss small flares; candidates are exported for verification.

facts.title: Limitation: Clouds, seasons, moon
facts.text: Cloudy months are only partially observed; STL removes average seasonality but not an abnormal season (snow, late monsoon).

facts.title: Limitation: Product breaks
facts.text: DMSP and VIIRS are not directly comparable: the harmonised long series (Li et al., 2020) is a modelled product, to be read for trends only.

facts.title: Limitation: NTL–GDP elasticity
facts.text: Estimated on 10 to 30 annual observations: wide intervals, possible instability, a non-causal relationship that varies with the level of development.

facts.title: Limitation: Access to electricity
facts.text: “Inhabited without light” ≠ “not connected”: a connected household with low consumption is invisible; the indicator depends strongly on the radiance threshold and the population data.

facts.title: Limitation: Administrative boundaries
facts.text: geoBoundaries/GAUL may differ from official boundaries; small ADM2 units are sensitive to light spilling over from neighbouring units.

facts.title: Limitation: Industrial zones
facts.text: Detection relies on thresholds: a power plant, a port or a large shopping centre can meet the signals; a dimly lit factory without visible emissions is missed. Sentinel-5P (≈ 5 km) and MODIS (1 km) are coarser than VIIRS: NO₂/SO₂/heat signals describe a neighbourhood, not a building.

facts.title: Limitation: Summer tourism
facts.text: The summer excess captures any rise in summer light (second homes, diaspora visits, festivals, construction), not only tourism; at high latitudes, very short summer nights reduce VIIRS observations. Ramadan changes night-time activity: the summers concerned are flagged.

facts.title: Convergence and concentration
facts.text: β-convergence (ADM2): β = -0.014 (CI -0.026 to -0.003, n = 264). β < 0 with a fully negative CI = convergence. Share of the leading region: 9.5% in 2014 → 9.7% in 2025; HHI 0.051.

facts.title: Elasticity (levels)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in levels: β = 4.19 (95% CI 1.02 to 7.36, R² = 0.54, n = 12, confidence medium: n = 12, significant but wide CI (6.34)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (growth rates)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in growth rates: β = 0.25 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.56, R² = 0.05, n = 11, confidence low: n = 11, not significant (p = 0.11)). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Elasticity (long DMSP–VIIRS series)
facts.text: Light–real GDP elasticity in long DMSP–VIIRS series: β = 1.06 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.25, R² = 0.89, n = 30, confidence high: n = 30, p < 0.01, narrow CI). +1% GDP ↔ +β% light.

facts.title: Out-of-sample tracking
facts.text: Out of sample, light-based growth has a correlation of -0.31 with official growth; mean absolute error 2.9 percentage point.

facts.title: Shock: COVID-19
facts.text: COVID-19 (2020-03-01 → 2021-06-30): trough of -9.0% on 2020-11-01, back to the pre-shock level after 10 months. Distinguishable from noise: yes.

facts.title: Detected breaks
facts.text: Structural breaks: 2020-03-01 (-7.6 %). Without a known event within ±6 months: 0.

facts.title: Regional impact of shocks
facts.text: Hardest-hit regions (trough): Tunis -23.2 % (covid19), Médenine -22.0 % (covid19), El Kef -20.2 % (covid19), Gabès -19.9 % (covid19), Béja -17.2 % (covid19).

facts.title: Gini and Theil
facts.text: Gini of light per capita (ADM2): 0.271 in 2014 → 0.272 in 2025 (change 0.001, bootstrap CI -0.026 to 0.020). Theil T 0.127; between-region share 37%.

facts.title: Population in the dark
facts.text: People in inhabited areas without detectable light: 0.06 M (13%) in 2014 → 0.07 M (12%) in 2025. Urban/rural light-per-capita ratio 0.5. Proxy of electricity access, sensitive to the threshold.

facts.title: Comparison with the World Bank
facts.text: Average gap between the share of people in lit areas and the World Bank electricity-access rate: -12.3 points.

facts.title: Method — Method
facts.text: Data: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) and annual VNL V2, harmonised DMSP–VIIRS, daily Black Marble, GHSL/WorldPop, Sentinel-5P NO₂/SO₂, MODIS LST, World Bank. Cleaning: pixels valid if cf_cvg ≥ 2, unit-month kept if ≥ 80% of pixels observed, spikes replaced, background and gas flares masked.

facts.title: Method — Dynamics
facts.text: Dynamics: robust STL on log(sum of lights), Theil–Sen trend + Mann–Kendall test, year-on-year growth, breaks by piecewise-linear segmentation with a BIC penalty.

facts.title: Method — Regions
facts.text: Regions: robust growth per unit, Growth/Decline class if |slope| ≥ 1%/yr and p < 0.10; β-convergence (robust OLS), σ-convergence, Herfindahl index.

facts.title: Method — GDP
facts.text: GDP: log(NTL) = α + β log(GDP) in levels and growth rates, HAC standard errors, DW/BP/JB diagnostics, out-of-sample tracking; experimental regional GDP allocated by light (γ = 1 and 0.5).

facts.title: Method — Shocks
facts.text: Shocks: trough = largest gap to the 12-month pre-shock level of the seasonally adjusted series, recovery = return to that level; daily Black Marble index (7-day rolling median).

facts.title: Method — Inequality
facts.text: Inequality: population-weighted Gini, Theil (between/within decomposition) and Lorenz; population in the dark = residents of pixels ≥ 5 people below 0.5 nW (sensitivity 0.25/0.5/1).

facts.title: Method — Industry
facts.text: Industry: six signals per pixel (light ≥ 5 nW, light per resident, GHSL non-residential built-up, Sentinel-5P NO₂ and SO₂, MODIS surface heat); pixels with ≥ 3 signals grouped into clusters; typology, confidence from concordant signals, precision/recall validation (official list or OSM).

facts.title: Method — Tourism
facts.text: Tourism: summer excess = log(peak-month light / shoulder-month light); net of the median of comparable units at the same latitude; tourist zone if ≥ +10% and significant over ≥ 3 summers; season index base 100; Ramadan flagged; validation with hotel nights.
